title: Engineering 2D Multifunctional Ultrathin Bismuthene for Multiple Photonic Nanomedicine

nodes.label: 2D bismuthene has not been used in nanomedicine because engineering it with the needed structure and composition is hard
Thin bismuthene should combine NIR photothermal conversion, red-light ROS generation and X-ray attenuation for imaging-guided PTT/PDT
Bulk layered Bi as feedstock: puckered layers with 5.62 A channels wide enough to take water (~3.2 A)
Water-mediated freeze-thaw intercalation/exfoliation with bath sonication, then NaBH4 reduction; organic-solvent free
Five freeze-thaw cycles (-80 C) with bath sonication exfoliate bulk Bi into oxidised nanosheets (bismuthene oxide)
NaBH4 reduction of the bismuthene-oxide sheets grows Bi nanoflakes on their surface, giving bismuthene
Free-standing lamellar nanosheets ~200 nm across and ~14 nm thick

notes: Spine: freeze-thaw exfoliation -> NaBH4 reduction -> thin Bi/Bi2O3 heterojunction sheets -> semiconducting (ROS, PDT branch) and NIR-absorbing (photothermal, PTT branch) -> joint in-vivo tumour eradication. Imaging (PA/CT), biosafety and BSA coating kept as side claims. Packet defect: paper Figure 4 (in-vitro cell work) is missing; packet F4 = paper Fig. 5 and F5 = paper Fig. 6 (captions say so). OCR cue classes tag most xy curves in F3 (d,f,h,i) and F5 (d-h) as micrograph with a scale bar; those panels were not cited (figs kept, panel_ids []). Audits: 14 nm AFM height vs "few-layer" framing; XPS 12:5 oxide:metal vs "monoelemental"; in-vivo laser power 7 vs 1 W cm-2; TUNEL/Ki-67 panels do not show the apoptosis claim. Wavelength of DPBF readout inconsistent (410 text / 421 axis / 470 caption). Lost: SI-only data (DLS, ICP-MS biodistribution, degradation, histology of organs).
